newsitem.title: USA: Ill. agency okays $105 mln school debt refinance.
newsitem.headline: Ill. agency okays $105 mln school debt refinance.

text.p: Illinois Educational Facilities Authority approved Loyola University Chicago's request for up to $105 million of financial assistance as part of an overall debt refinancing stemming from the division of the school and medical center into separate identities, Executive Director Thomas Conley said Friday.

In a meeting Thursday, the authority also gave preliminary approval to a $20 million request for financial assistance from Art Institute of Chicago and $17 million from Robert Morris College, Conley said.
The authority acts as a conduit, issuing tax-exempt revenue bonds and loaning the proceeds to the institutions at the same rates received, Conley noted.
Loyola plans to close on the debt refinancing in July, Conley added.
Final approval of the Robert Morris and Art Institute requests could come as early as the authority's July meeting if they are ready to proceed, Conley said.
Robert Morris' request comes as part of a planned relocation of their Chicago campus to larger quarters downtown under a longterm lease, Conley said.
